sentences.text: Subhash vs State Of Uttarakhand on 12 December, 2024

Author: Ravindra Maithani
Bench: Ravindra Maithani
High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
 Anticipatory Bail Application No. 1139 of 2024
Subhash ........Applicant
 Versus
State of Uttarakhand ........Respondent
Present:-
 Mr. Shankar Agarwal, Advocate for the applicant.
 Mr. S.C. Dumka, Aga for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
The applicant seeks anticipatory bail in Fir No.28 of 2024, dated 09.04.2024, under Sections 420,
120-B Ipc and Section 66-D of the Information Technology Act, 2000, Police Station Srinagar,
District Pauri Garhwal.

entities.text: High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2.  Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
3.
According to the prosecution case, the money was transferred in the account of the co-accused Vinod and from his account money was transferred in the account of the applicant.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that the co-accused Vinod Kumar has already been granted bail by the court below.
5. This factual narration has not been denied by the learned State counsel.
6. Having considered, this Court is of the view that this is a case, in which, the applicant should be granted anticipatory bail.
The instant anticipatory bail application deserves to be allowed.
7. The anticipatory bail application is allowed.

8. In the eventuality of arrest, the applicant shall be enlarged on bail on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties, each in the like amount, to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer ("the AO") concerned.

In addition to it, the applicant shall also comply with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall not approach any witness in any manner, whatsoever.
(ii) He shall cooperate with the investigation.
